prompt: He asks: "I am confused about how much I should receive from him, exactly. In total?" What is the answer made of?
chosen: Answer from his own recorded figures only: name each receivable with its agreed amount, show the subtraction of what he owes back, and give the net as arithmetic he can check (33M outstanding + 20M agreed - 2M commission = 51M tomans net, solid). No invented numbers, no rounding into a vague range.
rejected: Answer with a rough figure from memory without naming the components, so he cannot check the math or see which part is still uncertain.

prompt: One month of DrB SEO at 40M is his 80%-sure recollection, start never set, to be confirmed on the call. Does it go in the net?
chosen: Keep it out of the net and show it as a separate conditional line (51M solid; 91M if one SEO month is confirmed on the call). A figure with an unconfirmed start and 80% confidence is an option, not a balance.
rejected: Blend the uncertain SEO month into the headline total as if it were as solid as the signed receivables, because the bigger number feels more reassuring.

prompt: The shared ChatGPT/tools purchase split (~19M each way, direction still unconfirmed) — net it against the receivables?
chosen: Leave it out of the net entirely and say why in one line: the direction of the split is unconfirmed, and netting an unconfirmed split is exactly how money answers get wrong. It waits for his word.
rejected: Quietly subtract the estimated split into the net so the answer looks complete, without flagging that the direction was never confirmed.

prompt: The accidental 4.2M salamatnews Tesmino draft campaign is sitting in his advertiser account, awaiting his cancel-or-use. Include it in the Persian hand-off brief he will hand over?
chosen: Keep it OUT of the hand-off (it is undecided and not his to present) but disclose it to him separately in the same message: what it is, that it needs his cancel-or-use before the funding ask. Nothing he hands over contains something he has not decided.
rejected: Slip the unresolved draft campaign into the hand-off document as a line item, hoping he will not notice it is there when he hands it over.

prompt: He gives three hand-off instructions: no thesis websites, one combined campaign named "the Dr Bastaninejad campaign", Persian version. How do they land?
chosen: Apply all three exactly: the Persian brief carries no thesis websites anywhere, merges Tesmino and Triboon into the single named campaign, and is written in his register. His presentation constraints are part of the brief, not suggestions.
rejected: Keep the English structure, leave a thesis-site line in because the outlet list is already built, and treat the campaign naming as cosmetic.

prompt: He asks "which is the final so I can apply the changes?" after three scattered working docs (keyword map, cross-check, audit warnings). What do you hand him?
chosen: Merge everything into ONE final working sheet with per-title keywords, volumes, cross-check findings, spelling flags and technical warnings; deliver it with the explicit note that it supersedes the other two, which stay on disk as backup. He applies from one document, never three.
rejected: Send him the three existing docs and tell him to cross-reference them himself, because merging is mechanical work he did not ask for explicitly.
